units.title: Revision River Scene Repair
units.audience: Upper elementary writers who can draft a short scene and need a practical revision routine for clarity, pacing, and stronger reader cues.
units.summary: Students revise one short adventure scene by marking where the action slows, where the reader needs a clearer clue, and where a sentence can do more useful work.
objectives: Identify one strong moment, one confusing moment, and one slow moment in a draft.
Revise exposition into action, dialogue, or a precise clue label.
Explain one craft decision in a short revision note.
materials: One-page student draft or teacher-provided sample scene
Colored pencils or highlighters in three colors

lessonFlow.title: Map the Current Scene
lessonFlow.teacherMove: Model reading a short scene once for meaning and once for craft, marking a green star for the strongest moment, a blue question mark for confusion, and an orange pause for slow pacing.
lessonFlow.studentTask: Students reread their scene or sample and mark one strong moment, one confusing moment, and one slow moment.
lessonFlow.output: A marked draft with three revision targets.

lessonFlow.title: Trade Exposition for Evidence
lessonFlow.teacherMove: Show how a telling sentence can become a visible action, a line of dialogue, or a labeled clue that helps the reader infer what matters.
lessonFlow.studentTask: Students choose the confusing or slow moment and rewrite two to four sentences using action, dialogue, or a concrete clue.
lessonFlow.output: A revised scene section with clearer reader evidence.

lessonFlow.title: Write the Craft Note
lessonFlow.teacherMove: Prompt students to name the exact change they made and why it helps the reader follow the scene.
lessonFlow.studentTask: Students attach a sticky-note explanation that starts with, 'I changed...' and names the intended reader effect.
lessonFlow.output: A revised scene plus one craft-decision note.

teacherNotes: Keep the draft short enough for real revision inside the lesson; 150 to 250 words is enough.
If students do not have drafts, use a neutral sample about a ferry guide sorting mixed-up clue labels.
Treat peer feedback as reader response, not grading; students should point to a sentence and name what they understood.
Use the three-color code consistently so students can see revision as a sequence of decisions.
For reluctant writers, allow sentence replacement instead of full paragraph rewriting.
units.homeschoolAdaptation: Use a parent-child conference: the child reads the draft aloud, the parent marks only one confusing spot, and the child revises that spot before writing the craft note.
units.classroomManagement: Collect colored pencils before independent work starts, set a visible timer for each phase, and limit partner talk to one question and one suggestion per draft.
units.assessment: Check that each student marked three draft targets, revised one specific section, and wrote a craft note that explains the purpose of the revision.
units.printableOffer: Future printable pack idea: a Revision River scene repair map, color-code bookmark, sample scene, and classroom license version with extra peer-feedback slips.
units.safetyNote: No scary harm, no bullying, no romance, no weapons, no branded characters, no real child profiles.

units.title: Craft Academy Procedure Polish
units.audience: Upper elementary homeschool groups or classrooms practicing procedural writing, exposition control, and feedback that improves usability.
units.summary: Students revise a how-to page by testing whether a reader can follow each step, then tighten sequence words, remove filler exposition, and add useful cautions.
objectives: Sequence a procedure so each step can be followed without extra explanation.
Replace vague verbs and filler exposition with precise action language.
Use feedback to add one helpful margin note, caution, or materials clarification.
materials: Drafted how-to page or teacher-provided procedure sample
Checklist for precise verbs, sequence words, and materials

lessonFlow.title: Run the Reader Test
lessonFlow.teacherMove: Demonstrate following a procedure exactly as written, pausing when a missing material, unclear verb, or skipped sequence makes the step hard to complete.
lessonFlow.studentTask: Students trade procedures with a partner or adult and mark any place where the reader has to guess.
lessonFlow.output: A procedure draft with reader-test marks.

lessonFlow.title: Polish the Steps
lessonFlow.teacherMove: Model changing vague directions into precise steps with clear sequence words, exact materials, and only the background information the reader needs.
lessonFlow.studentTask: Students revise at least three steps by tightening verbs, adding sequence cues, or moving extra explanation into a short note.
lessonFlow.output: A clearer procedure with revised steps.

lessonFlow.title: Add the Useful Margin Note
lessonFlow.teacherMove: Show examples of margin notes that help the reader avoid confusion without taking over the whole page.
lessonFlow.studentTask: Students add one margin note, caution, or materials clarification based on reader feedback.
lessonFlow.output: A polished procedure page with one reader-tested support note.

teacherNotes: Choose low-stakes procedures such as folding a paper booklet, sorting an appendix card set, or building a paper compass marker.
Do not let students redesign the whole activity; the target is clearer writing, not a new project.
When feedback feels too broad, ask the reader to point to the exact step where guessing started.
Encourage precise verbs such as fold, align, label, compare, circle, and check.
Keep safety notes practical and classroom-based, such as asking an adult before using messy supplies.
units.homeschoolAdaptation: Have the child hand the procedure to an adult or sibling who silently follows the steps; the child records every pause as a revision target before rewriting.
units.classroomManagement: Pair students by draft length, keep materials at a central supply point, and require quiet reader tests before discussion so feedback is based on the written directions.
units.assessment: Review the final procedure for clear sequence, precise verbs, complete materials, and one margin note that responds to real reader feedback.
units.printableOffer: Future printable bundle idea: procedure test cards, craft academy revision checklist, margin-note strips, and a classroom license pack for repeated writing centers.
units.safetyNote: No scary harm, no bullying, no romance, no weapons, no branded characters, no real child profiles.
